<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" />{{rh|CHA. I.|ACCORDING TO S. LVKE.|137}}</noinclude>{{verse|chapter=1|verse=56}}† And {{sc|Marie}} taried with her about three moneths: and she returned into her house.

{{verse|chapter=1|verse=57}}† {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=The Gospel vpō the Natiuitie of S. Iohn Baptist Iun. 24. called Midsommer day.}}And Elisabeths ful time vvas come to be deliuered: and she bare a sonne. {{verse|chapter=1|verse=58}}† And her neighbours and kinsfolke heard that our Lord did magnifie his mercie vvith her, and they did congratulate her. {{verse|chapter=1|verse=59}}† And it came to passe: on the eight day they came to circumcise the childe, and they called him by his fathers name, Zacharie. {{verse|chapter=1|verse=60}}† And his mother ansvvering, said, Not so, but he shal be called Iohn. {{verse|chapter=1|verse=61}}† And they said to her, That there is none in thy kinred that is called by this name. {{verse|chapter=1|verse=62}}† And they made signes to his father, vvhat he vvould haue him called. {{verse|chapter=1|verse=63}}† And demaunding a vvriting table, he vvrote, saying, {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Lu. 1, 13.''}}* {{sup|‖}} Iohn is his name. And they al marueled. {{verse|chapter=1|verse=64}}† And forthvvith his mouth vvas opened, and his tonge, and he spake blessing God. {{verse|chapter=1|verse=65}}† And feare came vpon al their neighbours: and al these things vvere bruited ouer al the hil-countrie of Iewrie: {{verse|chapter=1|verse=66}}† and all that had heard, laid them vp in their hart, saying, what an one, trovv ye, shal this childe be? For the hand of our Lord vvas vvith him. {{verse|chapter=1|verse=67}}† And Zacharie his father vvas replenished vvith the Holy Ghost: and he prophecied, saying, {{verse|chapter=1|verse=68}}† {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ BENEDICTVS at Laudes.}}∷ ''{{sc|Blessed be ovr lord}} God of Israel: because he hath visited and vvrought the redemption of his people'':⊣ {{verse|chapter=1|verse=69}}† ''And hath erected the horne of saluation to vs, in the'' house of Dauid his seruant. {{verse|chapter=1|verse=70}}† ''As he spake by the mouth of his holy Prophets, that are from the beginning''. {{verse|chapter=1|verse=71}}† ''Saluation from our enemies, and from the hand of al that hate vs'': {{verse|chapter=1|verse=72}}† ''To worke mercie vvith our fathers: and to remember his holy testament'', {{verse|chapter=1|verse=73}}† {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Gen. 22, 6.''}}* ''The othe vvhich he svvare to Abraham our father'', {{verse|chapter=1|verse=74}}† ''that he vvould giue to vs, That vvithout feare being deliuered from the hand of our enemies, vve may serue him''. {{verse|chapter=1|verse=75}}† ''In holines and {{sup|‖}} iustice before him, al our daies''. {{verse|chapter=1|verse=76}}† ''And thou childe, shalt be called the Prophet of the Highest: for '' {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Mal. 3, 1.''}}* ''thou shalt goe before the face of our Lord to prepare his vvaies''. {{verse|chapter=1|verse=77}}† ''To giue knovvledge of saluation to his people, vnto remission of their sinnes'', {{verse|chapter=1|verse=78}}† {{sup|‖}} ''Through the bovvels of the mercie of our God, in vvhich the '' {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Zac. 3, 9. 6, 12. Mal. 4, 2.''}}* ''Orient, from on high, hath visited vs'', {{verse|chapter=1|verse=79}}† ''To illuminate them that sit in darkenes, and in the shadow of death: to direct our feete into the vvay of peace''. {{verse|chapter=1|verse=80}}† And the childe grew, and vvas strengthened in spirit, and vvas {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ Marke that he was a voluntarie Eremite, and chose to be solitarie from a childe, til he vvas to preach to the people, in so much that antiquitie counted him the first Eremite. Hiero. in vit. Pauli.}}∷ in the deserts vntil the day of his manifestation to Israel.
